docs.title: Documentation conventions
docs.text:
• Keep all project-specific facts, matrices, and exceptions on this page.
  • Keep reusable concepts, procedures, and design guidance in the topic pages.
  • Use assets/images/shared/ for media used across products and assets/images/<project-id>/ for product-specific media.
  • Use relative links so the documentation remains portable as a standalone repository or Git submodule.

docs.title: Choose a project
docs.text:
Start by identifying the product line. The product family has two main lines:

Product line User interface Product characteristics 201 Seven-segment display with mechanical push buttons Earlier gauge design. 202 Color display with touch input More compact and updated gauge design.

After selecting the product line, choose the firmware project that matches its MCU and Bluetooth hardware. This repository contains firmware for the 202 line. The central project overview describes the RW202 SAMD51 project and related BGM220 and PIC24F/BGM220P projects.

docs.title: Get source and submodules
docs.text: The repository uses Git submodules for shared code and BLE dependencies. The .gitmodules file currently uses HTTPS URLs, so HTTPS with Git Credential Manager is the simplest option for most developers. The main repository and private submodule repositories require authorized GitHub access.

docs.title: Clone with HTTPS
docs.text:
Run these commands in a terminal. Sign in through Git Credential Manager when prompted; do not put a personal access token directly in the clone URL.

git clone https://github.com/RwlsGroup/RW_202_UI_FW.git
cd RW_202_UI_FW
git submodule sync --recursive
git submodule update --init --recursive
git submodule status --recursive

The sync command applies the URLs from .gitmodules. The update command fetches and checks out the exact submodule revisions recorded by this repository. In the status output, each submodule should have a commit hash and should not begin with - (not initialized) or + (checked-out revision differs from the recorded revision).

If you already have a checkout, run the last three Git commands from the repository root to initialize or refresh submodules.

docs.title: Build the RW202 firmware in MPLAB X IDE
docs.text:
Use the project-compatible MPLAB X IDE version. MPLAB X IDE v6.35 is the version used by the current project build environment.

  1. Open the bootloader project: samd51_bootload_from_qspi/firmware/samd51_bootload_from_qspi.X/.
  2. Open the application project: dash_gauge_app/firmware/right_weigh_202_gauge_ui_fw.X/.
  3. Select the intended build configuration in each project. Use matching configurations for the bootloader and application.
  4. Build the bootloader first.
  5. Build the application second. Its post-build step consumes the outputs from both projects.

docs.title: Check the application build configuration
docs.text:
Before building the application, verify these settings in MPLAB X project properties:

  • Enable generation of the application .elf file. The build should also generate the map and HEX files needed by post-build processing.
  • The default application configuration is prepared with the Git commit ID and the Execute script after build command that runs the post-build packaging script. That script creates the OTA package and invokes the image-combination script.
  • The production application configuration does not currently include those local commit-ID and post-build command settings. If you build locally with production, configure and verify them first. The automated workflow supplies the required build metadata and runs the packaging steps itself.

The post-build process depends on the build utilities and signing configuration described in the project build documentation. Do not publish private signing material.

docs.title: Build outputs
docs.text: The curents scripts in folder scripts are used for build final output file.hex = bootload.bin + app.bin + checksum. The application post-build process also creates a versioned app.bin file for OTA updates.

docs.title: Program the device
docs.text:
• Program Microchip MCU firmware with a compatible Microchip programmer, such as PICkit 5. , and software MPLAB IPE.
  • Program Silicon Labs BGM220 Bluetooth-module firmware with a compatible SEGGER Flasher PRO setup.
  • Confirm the target MCU, board revision, module variant, image, and programming procedure before flashing.

docs.title: Provision Chassis Info
docs.text:
After first programming a gauge, use the corresponding printer application to write its Chassis Info included: serial number, hardware version, firmware version, number of sensors ...

For device with external flash: If a device must be returned to a completely unprovisioned state, program the approved reset_chassis_info image to clear the external flash data on products that use external flash. This repository includes PCB-0-54-x-ResetChassisInfoFw-v1-1.hex; verify the image is approved for the target hardware before use.

docs.title: Connect with the mobile application
docs.text:
The Right Weigh mobile application supports Android and iOS. Use it to connect to and add a device, read device parameters, view user instructions, and start an OTA firmware update. Keep the phone near the gauge and follow the app's prompts until the update completes.

play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.motus.rightweigh&pcampaignid=web_share

apps.apple.com/us/app/right-weigh-load-scales/id985400243

For shared build, protocol, and manufacturing practices, see the firmware, mobile integration, and supporting software guides.

docs.title: Shared Operating Model
docs.text: Embedded gauge products commonly combine a host MCU, peripheral sensors, a display, a BLE module, and a mobile application. The project comparison on the documentation home page identifies which components and functions apply to each product.

docs.title: Device architecture
docs.text:
The following diagram shows a typical gauge device. The main MCU reads the pressure sensors, controls the display, and exchanges data with the Bluetooth module. The Bluetooth module relays supported sensor information to the mobile application.

flowchart LR
    MCU["Main MCU"]
    BLE["Bluetooth module"]
    AirSensors["Four air pressure sensors"]
    AmbientSensor["Ambient pressure sensor"]
    Display["Display and touch input"]
    ExternalDevice["External device"]
    MobileApp["Mobile application"]

    MCU <-->|UART| BLE
    MCU <-->|I2C| AirSensors
    MCU <-->|I2C| AmbientSensor
    MCU <-->|Display interface| Display
    MCU <-->|Optional RS-232| ExternalDevice
    BLE <-->|Bluetooth Low Energy| MobileApp

docs.title: Typical runtime flow
docs.text:
1. Power is applied and the platform startup code runs.
  2. If a bootloader is present, it checks for its supported update or recovery conditions and transfers control to the application.
  3. The application initializes the required peripherals and product services.
  4. The host communicates with its BLE module using the interface defined for that project.
  5. A mobile application connects through the supported BLE services and displays the information exposed by the firmware.

docs.title: Firmware distribution flow
docs.text: Firmware is built for a specific product and version. The release process validates the package and publishes it to the approved distribution channel. A product may support factory programming, an in-field update, a recovery flow, or a subset of these options.

docs.title: RW202 build and release pipeline
docs.text:
Workflow Trigger Project-specific behavior docker-publish.yml Manual dispatch Builds and publishes the firmware build image to GitHub Container Registry. build_fw.yml Called by another workflow Checks out source and private submodules, builds bootloader and application, packages images, and uploads artifacts. test.yml Manual dispatch Calls the reusable workflow with the dev configuration. build.yml Push to master or manual dispatch Calls the reusable workflow with the production configuration. release.yml Push a v* tagPre-release: vxx.yy-RCzzRelease: vxx.yy.zz Builds production firmware and publishes a GitHub pre-release or stable release according to the tag.

The build produces a combined manufacturing Intel HEX image and a signed OTA binary. Build, test, and release workflows send completion notifications with run and artifact links to the configured Microsoft Teams channel.

flowchart TD
    Docker["Publish Docker build image<br/>Manual, one-time or when toolchain changes"] --> Registry["GitHub Container Registry"]
    Registry -. "reused by" .-> Shared["Reusable firmware build<br/>workflow_call: checkout source, build bootloader + app,<br/>package HEX + signed OTA BIN, upload artifacts"]

    Test["Test workflow<br/>Manual dispatch"] -->|"dev/test build"| Shared
    PR["Build workflow<br/>Pull request to main"] -->|"automated build"| Shared
    Tag["Release workflow<br/>Version tag"] -->|"production build"| Shared

    Shared --> TestArtifacts["Test build artifacts<br/>available to the team"]
    Shared --> PRArtifacts["Build artifacts<br/>available to the team"]
    Shared --> Release["Create GitHub pre-release or release"]
    Release --> ReleaseArtifacts["Release artifacts<br/>available to the team"]

    PR -. "completion notification" .-> Teams["Microsoft Teams channel"]
    Tag -. "completion notification" .-> Teams

The PR-to-main path shows the requested workflow design. In the current checked-in configuration, build.yml runs on pushes to master and manual dispatch; it does not yet declare a pull-request trigger for main.

OTA rollout note: OTA development began in 2026 and support is being introduced progressively. Not every product or firmware version supports every OTA step. Confirm compatibility for the exact device and firmware version before relying on an OTA update path.

Do not assume that bootloader behavior, memory layout, BLE services, or update transport is identical across projects. Refer to the central project overview and the shared topic guides before reusing a procedure.

docs.title: RW202 manufacturing process
docs.text:
This simplified flow is based on Documentation/MfgProcessInteraction/202GaugeMfgProcessInteraction.drawio (revision 1.2). It shows the first-boot path for factory programming and Chassis Info provisioning, followed by the normal customer startup path.

flowchart TD
    Program["Program MCU and BLE module firmware<br/>FirstBoot flag is set"] --> Power["Apply power"]
    Power --> FirstBoot{"FirstBoot flag set?"}

    FirstBoot -- Yes --> Diagnostics["Show diagnostic screen<br/>with touch-screen test"]
    SensorReadings["Barometric and air-sensor PSI readings are visible"] -.-> Diagnostics
    Diagnostics --> TouchTest["Operator presses the final Test button"]
    TouchTest --> ConfigureBT["Start Bluetooth interface<br/>in Configure Chassis Info mode"]
    ConfigureBT --> ChassisInfo{"Chassis Info already configured?"}
    ChassisInfo -- Yes --> ClearFlag["Clear FirstBoot flag"]
    ChassisInfo -- No --> Waiting["Show waiting-for-Chassis-Info screen"]
    Waiting --> MfgApp["Manufacturing app writes Chassis Info over Bluetooth"]
    MfgApp --> AllConfigured{"All Chassis Info configured?"}
    AllConfigured -- No --> Waiting
    AllConfigured -- Yes --> ClearFlag
    ClearFlag --> SystemInfo["Show System Info with current Chassis Info"]
    SystemInfo --> PowerOff["Operator disconnects gauge power"]

    FirstBoot -- No --> CustomerBT["Start Bluetooth interface<br/>in Customer API mode"]
    CustomerBT --> WizardComplete{"Setup Wizard complete?"}
    WizardComplete -- No --> SetupWizard["Start gauge in Setup Wizard mode"]
    WizardComplete -- Yes --> Measurement["Start gauge in Measurement mode"]
    SetupWizard --> Measurement

    ConfigureBT -. "May overwrite existing Chassis Info" .-> MfgApp

The manufacturing application can overwrite existing Chassis Info while the gauge is in the configuration mode. Product setup details and manufacturing tool instructions should follow the approved product-specific procedure.

docs.title: Version format
docs.text:
Firmware releases use the common format:

Major_version.minor_version.build_version
Component Meaning Major_version Identifies the device hardware family/version. It distinguishes firmware built for different product hardware. minor_version Identifies a major software generation or significant firmware change for that hardware family. build_version Identifies a build or release within the major/minor version.

For example, 54.9.4 means hardware family 54, software generation 9, build 4. A pre-release label may be written as 54.9-RC4; the numeric OTA package version is 54.9.4.

docs.title: Product hardware mapping
docs.text:
Product line Hardware major version BLE module Version pattern 202 Dash Gauge 54 BGM220S 54.<minor>.<build> 201 Gauge 52 BGM220P 52.<minor>.<build> Additional device 1 TBD TBD TBD Additional device 2 TBD TBD TBD Additional device 3 TBD TBD TBD

The three additional rows are placeholders for product lines that will be added to this documentation. Confirm the hardware version and BLE module from the approved hardware definition before assigning a version series.

docs.title: When to increment each component
docs.text:
• Keep Major_version tied to the hardware family. Use a different major value when firmware compatibility is specific to a different hardware family.
  • Increment minor_version for a significant firmware change or new software generation while the hardware major remains the same.
  • Increment build_version for a build or release within the same hardware and software generation.

For example, a major firmware architecture change on the 202 hardware can move from 54.8.3 to 54.9.1. The major value remains 54 because the hardware family is unchanged; the minor value advances because the software changed significantly, and the build sequence starts at 1 for that minor release. The RW202 OTA work is an example of such a change because it introduced a new OTA flow and significant memory-layout changes.

The authoritative RW202 values are RW202_MAJOR_VER, RW202_MINOR_VER, and RW202_RC_VER in dash_gauge_app/firmware/src/dash_gauge_fw_version.h. The automated build derives the displayed pre-release and numeric OTA version from these values. See the RW202 project and release pipeline overview.

docs.title: Release notes by product line
docs.text: Maintain a separate release-note table for each hardware family. Record the published version and the user-visible or compatibility-relevant changes. Keep implementation details in the relevant firmware documentation.

docs.title: 202 Dash Gauge — Hardware 54, BGM220S
docs.text: Version Release notes 54.9.1 (RC1) Introduced the MCUboot Mini OTA and recovery flow. Expanded the bootloader region and moved application start to 0x10000; added firmware backup/check/verification, BLE security and mobile PIN unlock, QSPI DMA, watchdog support, and moved FirstBoot state to NVM user row. Signature verification and image decoding were not supported in this release candidate. 54.9.2 (RC2) Added sensor-count support through the NumOfSensors characteristic and Chassis Info. The mobile app can read and write the configured sensor count; the gauge uses the configured count in its display. Also clears Chassis Info on first boot and includes the 54.8 changes. 54.9.3 (RC3) Updated the MPLAB X build environment and CI/CD workflow. Added separate default, dev, and release configurations, build-time commit/debug metadata, and a BLE characteristic update for device-change notification. 54.9.4 (RC4, current source) Updated the NCP host integration for the newer BGM220S firmware, including its BLE security service and GATT database.

BGM220P UART pins, baud rate, flow control, module power/reset controls, and supported module firmware. docs.text: The 201 schematic was not available alongside the referenced 202 block diagram during this documentation update. Add the schematic/BOM revision, MCU part number, sensor configuration, connector pinout, and programming instructions from the controlled 201 design package before using this page as a manufacturing reference.

docs.title: Identification
docs.text:
Item 202 Dash Gauge Hardware version 54 Main MCU ATSAMD51J19A BLE module BGM220S User interface Color display with touch input Pressure sensing Four air-pressure sensors plus a barometric sensor

The product-level view below is based on the available 202 block diagram. Confirm exact component revisions and signal names against the released schematic and BOM.

Figure: 202 Dash Gauge schematic block diagram.

docs.title: Main connections
docs.text:
• The ATSAMD51J19A is the main controller for sensing, application logic, and display control.
  • The BGM220S provides BLE connectivity. The MCU-to-module application link is UART; confirm pin assignment and serial settings in the detailed schematic and firmware configuration.
  • Four air-pressure sensors connect through an I²C multiplexer. The firmware identifies these as the four pressure-sensor inputs.
  • A separate barometric pressure sensor connects on the barometric I²C bus.
  • The color display and touch input connect to the MCU through the display and touch signals shown in the block diagram.
  • An RS-232 interface is shown for external serial equipment. Its use depends on the board configuration and enabled firmware feature.
  • External serial flash is shown for nonvolatile storage. Confirm the exact part and SPI/QSPI mode against the released schematic and driver configuration.
  • Power input and regulation are shown in the block diagram; detailed power limits belong in the electrical design documentation.

docs.title: Firmware-facing notes
docs.text: Firmware currently contains drivers for four MS5837 pressure sensors and an MS5637 barometric sensor, with I²C mux channel selection for the pressure sensors. The mux header defines PCA9545A write/read addresses and eight selectable channel identifiers; the 202 sensing path uses four channels. Consult the firmware pages for bus handling and sensor-data processing.

docs.title: Revision-specific records
docs.text: Add the approved schematic revision, BOM revision, display part number, touch-controller part number, external flash part number, connector pinouts, and programming procedure when those controlled design records are available. Do not infer exact pin numbers from this functional block diagram.

docs.title: Hardware Architecture
docs.text: This page describes the shared device architecture. Product-specific parts and differences are listed in 201 Gauge and 202 Dash Gauge. Use the approved schematic and BOM for exact pin assignments, electrical limits, and board revisions.

docs.title: System overview
docs.text:
The main MCU reads pressure sensors, runs the gauge application, and controls the display. A separate Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) module communicates with the MCU over UART and provides the wireless link to the mobile application. The MCU may also communicate with external equipment over an RS-232 interface.

flowchart LR
  App[Mobile application] <-->|Bluetooth Low Energy| BLE[Bluetooth module]
  BLE <-->|UART| MCU[Main MCU]
  MCU <-->|I2C| Mux[I2C multiplexer]
  Mux <-->|I2C channels| Air[Four air pressure sensors]
  MCU <-->|I2C| Ambient[Ambient pressure sensor]
  MCU -->|Display interface| Display[Display]
  Input[Touch or physical keys] --> MCU
  MCU <-->|UART through RS-232 transceiver| External[Optional external equipment]
  MCU <-->|SPI or QSPI, board dependent| Flash[External nonvolatile memory]

The drawing shows the functional relationships. It does not define connector pinouts, voltage levels, bus rates, or exact peripheral instances.

docs.title: MCU connections
docs.text: Subsystem MCU connection Purpose Design notes BLE module UART Exchanges commands and data with the BLE module; the module provides the mobile link. Document baud rate, flow control, framing, and UART instance per board revision. Four air pressure sensors I²C through a multiplexer Reads separate pressure sensors that may share the same I²C address. Select one mux channel before addressing its sensor. The 202 implementation uses four channels. Ambient pressure sensor I²C Reads barometric pressure for environmental compensation and related calculations. The 202 schematic shows a dedicated barometric I²C bus. Display Board-specific display interface Presents measurements and device status. Interface varies by product; consult the product page and schematic. User input Touch interface or GPIO-connected keys Receives user selections and setup actions. 202 uses touch input; 201 uses mechanical buttons. External equipment UART plus an RS-232 transceiver, when fitted Exchanges serial data with compatible equipment. RS-232 electrical signaling requires a transceiver; MCU UART pins are logic-level signals. External memory SPI/QSPI, board dependent Stores data such as calibration or update images where implemented. Verify memory part, bus mode, and address map for each product.

docs.title: I²C pressure-sensor topology
docs.text:
Each sensor is addressed by the MCU using its I²C controller. The mux connects the shared upstream bus to one downstream channel at a time, allowing multiple sensors with the same address to coexist. The ambient pressure sensor is a separate device; its bus relationship must follow the product schematic.

For the 202 implementation, firmware defines four air-pressure sensors and selects mux channels while probing and sampling them. It also initializes a separate barometric sensor. See 202 Dash Gauge and I²C and I²C Multiplexer.

docs.title: BLE and mobile data path
docs.text: The MCU and BLE module form separate processing and radio responsibilities. The MCU obtains and processes sensor data, then exchanges application data with the BLE module over UART. The module exposes the Bluetooth connection used by the mobile application to view sensor information and perform supported device functions. BLE services, characteristic definitions, and framing are firmware-version specific; see Bluetooth communication.

docs.title: RS-232 connection
docs.text: Where fitted and enabled, the MCU uses a UART connected through an RS-232 transceiver to communicate with external equipment. The interface is optional and is controlled by the product hardware and firmware configuration. See RS-232 communication.

docs.title: Product-specific hardware
docs.text:
• 201 Gauge: hardware version 52, BGM220P BLE module, seven-segment display, and mechanical buttons.
  • 202 Dash Gauge: hardware version 54, BGM220S BLE module, color display, and touch input.

docs.title: Design records to maintain
docs.text: For every board revision, keep the MCU and module part numbers, schematic and BOM revisions, connector pinout, signal direction, voltage domain, programming/debug method, and supported firmware version together. Treat changes to sensor count, mux topology, display interface, BLE module, storage device, or serial interface as product compatibility changes.

docs.title: Firmware Architecture
docs.text: Embedded products in this documentation are organized around a bootloader and an application, with a separate BLE module firmware where present. Keep each image's responsibilities and upgrade boundaries explicit.

docs.title: Component boundaries
docs.text:
• Bootloader: startup checks, application handoff, and the update or recovery operations implemented by that target.
  • Application: product workflows, user interface, sensor processing, and communication with peripherals and the BLE module.
  • BLE module firmware: radio behavior, BLE services, and the module-side host interface. This is a separately versioned component when independently updated.

Some products combine or omit these components. The project overview is authoritative for which components are present.

docs.title: Firmware documentation checklist
docs.text:
Browse the focused pages for peripherals, UART, I²C and its multiplexer, SPI/QSPI, OTA support, memory layout, external flash, update and recovery, pressure calculation and calibration, display and input, Bluetooth communication, and RS-232 communication.

For each project, document the target part, toolchain, build configuration, memory layout, image format, boot sequence, version source, and compatibility requirements. For OTA, also document the transport, staging area, validation, activation, rollback/recovery behavior, and user-visible status.

Do not assume that a host application's OTA capability also updates the BLE module. Treat each independently updated image as a separate versioned component and identify compatible combinations.

docs.title: Shared Build and Release Practices
docs.text: Use a repeatable build pipeline for each embedded project. Keep project-specific workflow files, tool versions, secrets, and triggers in that project's repository documentation.

docs.title: Build stages
docs.text:
1. Check out the intended source revision and its pinned dependencies.
  2. Select the target, build configuration, and toolchain explicitly.
  3. Build each independently versioned firmware component.
  4. Validate that expected images exist and are non-empty; record the source commit and version.
  5. Package the outputs in the formats required for factory programming and field updates.
  6. Publish artifacts with clear names, retention, access controls, and traceability to the source revision.

docs.title: Release controls
docs.text:
• Validate release tags and embedded image versions before publishing.
  • Sign update images when the product's update design requires a signature; protect signing keys as secrets.
  • Keep development, test, pre-release, and production artifacts distinguishable.
  • Publish checksums or provenance when required by the product release process.
  • Notify the team with links to the completed build, release notes, and artifacts.
  • Document rollback, recovery, and artifact retention policies per product.

docs.title: Project-specific pipelines
docs.text: The workflow currently configured for RW202 is summarized in the central project overview. Record project-specific triggers and artifact names in that overview when they are verified.

docs.title: Firmware Peripherals
docs.text:
This section describes the firmware-facing peripheral interfaces used by the gauge products. Exact pins, peripheral instances, timing, and enabled features are defined by each board configuration.

Interface Typical role Details UART MCU-to-BLE module and optional serial equipment UART I²C Pressure sensors, ambient sensor, and I²C mux I²C and I²C Multiplexer SPI/QSPI External serial flash where fitted SPI and QSPI

docs.title: Shared implementation guidance
docs.text: Keep bus ownership explicit, check transfer completion and error status, and avoid accessing a shared bus concurrently without the project’s synchronization mechanism. Peripheral configuration and supported devices can differ between product lines; always trace behavior to the target configuration and schematic.

docs.title: RS-232 Communication
docs.text:
Some device configurations provide an optional serial connection to external equipment. Firmware uses a UART at MCU logic levels and a transceiver converts those signals to RS-232 electrical levels.

The 202 source feature header defines FEATURE_USE_RS232_INTERFACE as disabled in the inspected configuration. Therefore, the interface should be considered optional and configuration-dependent.

For each enabled product, document the connector and pinout, transceiver, baud rate, parity, stop bits, flow control, protocol specification, message units, timeouts, and error behavior. Keep the external protocol independent of the MCU-to-BLE UART protocol.

docs.title: Uses
docs.text: The MCU UART is used for the host link to the BLE module. Some board configurations can also route a UART through an RS-232 transceiver to external equipment. These links have separate protocol and configuration requirements even when they use the same MCU peripheral family.

docs.title: Data path
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  App[Gauge application] <-->|UART frames| BLE[BLE module]
  App <-->|Optional UART frames| XCVR[RS-232 transceiver]
  XCVR <-->|RS-232 electrical link| Device[External equipment]

Document the UART instance, TX/RX pins, baud rate, parity, stop bits, flow control, buffering, framing, and timeout behavior for each board. Do not connect MCU logic-level UART signals directly to an RS-232 line; the transceiver performs the required electrical conversion.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text: Define how framing errors, overrun, disconnects, and partial frames are handled. Keep BLE-module framing separate from any external-device protocol. Add protocol-specific details to Bluetooth communication and RS-232 communication.

docs.title: Current use
docs.text: The 202 block diagram includes external serial flash, and application source references QSPI flash for calibration data and OTA image handling. The block diagram labels the memory as SPI flash; therefore, confirm the exact MCU peripheral mode, flash part, wiring, and memory map against the released schematic and board configuration before using this page for low-level implementation work.

docs.title: Documentation requirements
docs.text:
For each supported board, record the flash manufacturer and part number, bus mode, clock limits, chip-select behavior, address width, erase size, page/program size, protection settings, and any DMA/cache constraints. Keep the flash driver abstraction separate from application data formats.

Related pages: External Flash, Memory Layout, and OTA Support.

docs.title: Bus roles
docs.text: The 202 firmware reads four MS5837 air-pressure sensors and a separate MS5637 barometric sensor. The four pressure sensors are selected through an I²C multiplexer because they share the pressure-sensor bus topology; the barometric sensor is initialized and checked separately. Other products may use a different sensor set or bus arrangement.

docs.title: Multiplexer operation
docs.text:
The firmware exposes I2CMux_selectChannel() and PCA9545A address constants in its I²C mux interface. The channel enum contains channels 0 through 7. The 202 pressure-sensor code selects mux channels while probing and sampling the four sensors. The block diagram maps the four sensor branches to mux channels 0–3.

Typical access sequence:

  1. Acquire the bus lock if the bus is shared by concurrent tasks.
  2. Select the mux channel associated with the target sensor.
  3. Perform the sensor transaction and check its result.
  4. Release the bus lock on every success or error path.

docs.title: Sensor handling
docs.text: The pressure-sensor implementation checks connectivity, resets/converts/reads sensor data, and handles transfer or CRC status through the sensor drivers. Preserve per-sensor identity when storing results. A mux-selection or I²C failure should not be represented as a valid pressure reading.

docs.title: Board-specific details to record
docs.text: Record bus speed, MCU controller instance, pull-up voltage, mux address configuration, channel-to-sensor mapping, sensor addresses, and recovery behavior for a stuck bus in the product design documentation.

docs.title: Display and Input
docs.text: Display and input are product-specific. The 202 uses a color display with touch input; the 201 uses a seven-segment display and mechanical buttons.

docs.title: Display responsibilities
docs.text: The application presents measurements, device state, warnings, and setup workflows. Document the display controller and MCU interface, refresh behavior, brightness control, startup screen, measurement units, and behavior when sensor data is unavailable.

docs.title: Input responsibilities
docs.text:
Touch or button events select screens and invoke supported actions. Document event mapping, debouncing/filtering, long-press behavior, input lockout, and the user feedback shown for rejected actions. Keep safety-relevant thresholds and calibration authorization rules in the product requirements.

See the product hardware pages for known interface differences. Exact controller and pin-level details must come from each approved schematic and firmware configuration.

docs.title: Bluetooth Communication
docs.text: The BLE module provides the radio connection to the mobile application, while the main MCU owns gauge sensing and product behavior. The MCU-to-module link is UART. The module part differs by product: BGM220P on 201 and BGM220S on 202.

docs.title: Documented protocol areas
docs.text:
For each compatible firmware and mobile-app release, maintain the BLE service/characteristic UUIDs, roles and permissions, advertising identity, connection behavior, payload encoding, command/response framing, notification rules, and error/status codes. Record the UART-side framing between the MCU and BLE module separately from the over-the-air GATT protocol.

The 202 application source includes SMP-style image-upload packet parsing for an OTA path. Confirm the active BLE characteristic, complete response path, and production support in the corresponding module and mobile-app versions before treating this as an available user feature.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Track the compatible combinations of product hardware, MCU application, BLE module firmware, and mobile application. Application OTA support does not by itself imply that BLE module firmware is updated.

docs.title: Pressure acquisition
docs.text: On the 202 target, firmware reads four MS5837 pressure sensors and a separate MS5637 barometric sensor. Sensor drivers perform the device-specific conversion and compensation; application code retains each sensor's identity and units for downstream calculations.

docs.title: Calculation documentation
docs.text:
For each released algorithm, record:

  • raw sensor quantities and units;
  • temperature and barometric compensation inputs;
  • conversion equations and constants;
  • filtering, plausibility limits, and invalid-data handling;
  • mapping from sensor channels to physical axle/vehicle positions;
  • output units, rounding, and display/mobile presentation.

Do not treat the sensor pressure reading as a calibrated vehicle weight without the product-specific calibration and conversion model.

docs.title: Calibration data
docs.text: Calibration workflow and stored values are product-specific. Document the authorized calibration procedure, required reference loads, acceptance limits, storage location, data version, and reset/recovery behavior. The 202 source includes calibration data access to QSPI flash; verify the exact layout and persistence rules for the target build.

docs.title: OTA Support
docs.text: OTA support is being introduced progressively from 2026. Availability depends on product, bootloader/application versions, and mobile-app support. Check the release notes and compatibility information for the target device before planning an update.

docs.title: Update components
docs.text:
The bootloader is responsible for startup validation, application handoff, and the update/recovery behavior implemented for that target. The application and BLE module are distinct firmware components; an application OTA path must not be assumed to update the BLE module.

The 202 application source contains an image-upload path using an SMP-style frame and QSPI write helpers. This source alone does not establish the full production activation, validation, rollback, or recovery behavior. Document those guarantees from the corresponding bootloader and mobile-app implementation.

docs.title: Related details
docs.text:
• Memory Layout
  • External Flash
  • Update and Recovery

For each released combination, document image format, target hardware, version compatibility, transport, integrity/authenticity checks, activation rules, power-loss behavior, and recovery procedure.

docs.title: Firmware Memory Layout
docs.text: Memory boundaries are bootloader- and hardware-version-specific. Use the linker scripts, bootloader configuration, and released build artifacts as the source of truth; do not copy addresses between products.

docs.title: Required map
docs.text:
Maintain a table for each target showing:

Region Start/end address Owner Erase/write constraints Bootloader From target linker/configuration Bootloader Preserve during application update unless an explicitly supported bootloader update is used. Active application From target linker/configuration Application Must match the bootloader handoff and vector expectations. Staging/update image From target configuration OTA/update path Must fit the largest supported image and meet flash erase/program rules. Persistent device data From target configuration Application Define schema, migration, and reset behavior.

The combined factory image and the OTA application image can have different contents and address assumptions. See Build and Release and Update and Recovery.

docs.title: Update flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  Start[Mobile app starts supported update] --> Check[Check device and image compatibility]
  Check -->|Supported| Transfer[Transfer image to device]
  Check -->|Unsupported| Stop[Stop and report compatibility error]
  Transfer --> Stage[Stage image in configured memory]
  Stage --> Verify[Verify image using target implementation]
  Verify -->|Valid| Activate[Request activation or reboot]
  Verify -->|Invalid| Reject[Reject image and retain safe state]
  Activate --> Boot[Bootloader validates and starts application]

This is a conceptual workflow. Exact validation, activation, rollback, and status reporting must be documented for each released implementation; the diagram does not imply that every step is currently enabled on every product.

docs.title: Recovery information to maintain
docs.text:
Document recovery behavior for interrupted transfer, power loss during flash operations, invalid image, failed application startup, and an unreachable BLE link. Include the required programming tool and factory image for restoring a device. Never assume rollback exists unless the target bootloader implements and verifies it.

OTA functionality is being introduced from 2026 and will expand across product versions over time. Check the specific release notes before performing an update.

docs.title: External Flash
docs.text: External flash may hold calibration or other persistent data and can serve as OTA staging storage on supported targets. Actual use and capacity are product-specific.

docs.title: Design and firmware requirements
docs.text:
• Identify the exact flash part, capacity, interface mode, and board revision.
  • Publish a memory map with reserved regions, offsets, erase blocks, and page sizes.
  • Define data format, versioning, integrity checks, and migration behavior for persistent records.
  • Prevent concurrent operations from corrupting calibration or an in-progress update.
  • Define behavior for interrupted erase/program operations and failed verification.

The 202 source references QSPI for calibration data and OTA upload writes. Verify the part and layout from the released board and firmware configuration before servicing or provisioning devices.

docs.title: Mobile Application
docs.text: The Right Weigh mobile application supports Android and iOS and communicates with compatible devices over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE).

docs.title: Scale Detail and firmware updates
docs.text:
Each time the user opens Scale Detail, the app scans for the device and reads its information, including its firmware version. The app compares that version with the firmware version available online. If a compatible update is available, the app displays a firmware update link. The user can select it to download the firmware and start the OTA update.

OTA support is under development and being introduced progressively from 2026. Availability depends on the device and firmware version.

docs.title: Shared Firmware Distribution Guidance
docs.text: When firmware is distributed through a web portal or cloud catalog, treat the catalog as part of the controlled release path.

docs.title: Recommended release metadata
docs.text: Each published package should identify the product and hardware compatibility, firmware component, version, release channel, publication date, and source release. Keep host-MCU images distinct from BLE module images unless the update package intentionally contains both.

docs.title: Release and availability controls
docs.text:
• Publish only artifacts produced by the approved release pipeline.
  • Validate package identity and compatibility before making a version available to customers.
  • Keep development and test images out of production catalogs.
  • Provide a clear path to withdraw a faulty package and restore the previous supported version.
  • Coordinate catalog availability with mobile app behavior and release communications.

Document actual portal ownership, API contracts, and customer instructions in the project or service documentation; those details are not shared across all products by default.

docs.title: Shared Tooling and Manufacturing Guidance
docs.text: Toolchains and factory processes differ by MCU and hardware revision. Keep reusable guidance here and list exact versions, commands, and approved equipment in each project's documentation.

docs.title: Development and CI tools
docs.text: For each project, document the IDE, compiler, device packs or SDK, host utilities, container image, and supported operating systems. Pin or record versions used by CI so a build can be reproduced. Keep credentials and signing keys in the approved secret store.

docs.title: Manufacturing and provisioning
docs.text: Document the programming image, programmer model, fixture, programming mode, device-specific provisioning fields, and verification steps. Identify which utility writes each field and how programming success is checked. Version-control manufacturing software and configuration where permitted.

docs.title: Media and diagrams
docs.text:
Store documentation media under assets/images/:

assets/images/
├── shared/                         # reused across products
├── rw202-samd51/                   # RW202-specific media
├── bgm220-ble-firmware/            # BLE module firmware media
└── pic24f-bgm220p/                 # PIC24F/BGM220P media

Use relative links in Markdown. Keep editable source files with exported diagrams where practical. Avoid placing credentials, private keys, or customer data in documentation media.
